gestalt.title: Closure
gestalt.summary: The mind completes incomplete shapes; you don't need to draw every line.

gestalt.title: Common Fate
gestalt.summary: Elements moving together are perceived as related.

gestalt.title: Common Region
gestalt.summary: Items in the same bounded region (card, panel) are perceived as a unit.

gestalt.title: Continuity / Good Continuation
gestalt.summary: The eye follows smooth lines and curves; align elements to continuous axes.

gestalt.title: Figure / Ground
gestalt.summary: Establish clear figure-ground separation so users know what to focus on.

gestalt.title: Focal Point
gestalt.summary: Every screen needs one primary focal point. More than one creates competition.

gestalt.title: Visual Hierarchy
gestalt.summary: Establish a clear reading order with size, weight, color, and spacing.

gestalt.title: Proximity
gestalt.summary: Group related items by spatial closeness; separate unrelated items with whitespace.

gestalt.title: Similarity
gestalt.summary: Visually similar elements are perceived as related, even when far apart.

gestalt.title: Symmetry & Balance
gestalt.summary: Symmetric compositions feel stable; asymmetric ones feel dynamic.

heuristics.title: Consistency and Standards
heuristics.summary: Follow platform conventions. Same things should look and behave the same way.

heuristics.title: Error Prevention
heuristics.summary: Prevent errors before they happen via good design and constraints.

heuristics.title: Help Users Recover From Errors
heuristics.summary: Error messages: plain language, problem stated, solution suggested.

heuristics.title: Flexibility and Efficiency of Use
heuristics.summary: Accelerators for experts that don't get in the way of novices.

heuristics.title: Help and Documentation
heuristics.summary: Even better if no help is needed, but provide it for complex tasks.

heuristics.title: Match Between System and Real World
heuristics.summary: Use language and concepts familiar to your users, not internal jargon.

heuristics.title: Aesthetic and Minimalist Design
heuristics.summary: Remove what isn't needed. Every extra element competes for attention.

heuristics.title: Recognition Rather Than Recall
heuristics.summary: Minimize memory load by making options, actions, and information visible.

heuristics.title: Visibility of System Status
heuristics.summary: Always keep users informed about what's happening through appropriate feedback.

heuristics.title: Trust and Credibility
heuristics.summary: Polish, transparency, and predictability build trust. Cheap-looking UI loses users.

heuristics.title: Respect User Autonomy
heuristics.summary: Don't dark-pattern users into actions they didn't choose.

heuristics.title: User Control and Freedom
heuristics.summary: Provide clearly marked emergency exits — undo, cancel, back.

a11y.title: Accessible Names for Controls
a11y.summary: Every interactive element has an accessible name (visible label, aria-label, or aria-labelledby).

a11y.title: Image Alt Text
a11y.summary: Meaningful images need descriptive alt; decorative images need alt=''.

a11y.title: Correct ARIA Roles
a11y.summary: ARIA roles must match the element's actual behavior.

a11y.title: Autocomplete on Form Fields
a11y.summary: Use autocomplete tokens to help password managers and assistive tech.

a11y.title: Captions and Transcripts
a11y.summary: Pre-recorded video has captions; audio has transcript.

a11y.title: Text Color Contrast
a11y.summary: Body text ≥4.5:1, large text ≥3:1, UI components ≥3:1 against background.

a11y.title: Color Is Not the Only Channel
a11y.summary: Don't rely on color alone to convey meaning.

a11y.title: Logical Focus Order
a11y.summary: Tab order follows visual reading order; no traps or skips.

a11y.title: Visible Focus Indicators
a11y.summary: Keyboard users must see where focus is at all times.

a11y.title: Identify Form Errors Accessibly
a11y.summary: Errors associated with the relevant field via aria-describedby; error summary at top of form.

a11y.title: Form Labels
a11y.summary: Every form field has a programmatically associated, persistent visible label.

a11y.title: Heading Hierarchy
a11y.summary: One h1 per page; never skip levels (h2 → h4).

a11y.title: Windows High Contrast Mode
a11y.summary: Test in forced-colors mode; ensure UI remains usable.

a11y.title: Full Keyboard Operability
a11y.summary: Every interactive element must be reachable AND operable by keyboard alone.

a11y.title: Document Language
a11y.summary: <html lang='...'> and lang attributes on foreign-language inline content.

a11y.title: Live Regions for Dynamic Content
a11y.summary: Announce dynamic updates (toasts, errors, search results) to screen readers.

a11y.title: Honor prefers-reduced-motion
a11y.summary: Disable or reduce non-essential motion when user prefers reduced motion.

a11y.title: No Flashing Content
a11y.summary: No content flashes more than 3 times per second.

a11y.title: Non-Text Contrast
a11y.summary: UI components and graphical elements need ≥3:1 against adjacent colors.

a11y.title: Screen-Reader-Only Text
a11y.summary: Use sr-only utility for context that's visual-only obvious.

a11y.title: Semantic HTML First
a11y.summary: Use the right element for the job. ARIA is a fallback, not a starting point.

a11y.title: Session Timeout Warnings
a11y.summary: Warn users before timeout; offer to extend session.

a11y.title: Skip Navigation Link
a11y.summary: Provide a 'Skip to main content' link as the first focusable element.

a11y.title: Touch Target Size
a11y.summary: Interactive targets ≥44×44px (iOS) / 48×48dp (Material).

a11y.title: Zoom and Reflow
a11y.summary: Page must work at 200% zoom and reflow at 320 CSS px width.

interaction.title: Click Targets Match Affordance
interaction.summary: Visual affordance and click area must match exactly.

interaction.title: Confirm Destructive Actions
interaction.summary: Irreversible destructive actions require confirmation OR robust undo.

interaction.title: Drag-and-Drop Has Keyboard Equivalent
interaction.summary: Every drag-drop interaction has buttons or shortcuts for keyboard users.

interaction.title: Feedback Latency Tiers
interaction.summary: <100ms feels instant. 100-300ms feels snappy. 300ms-1s needs feedback. >1s needs progress.

interaction.title: Dont Block on Validation
interaction.summary: Validate inline as user types or on blur. Don't block submit until errors are visible.

interaction.title: Hover Is Not a Requirement
interaction.summary: Hover-only interactions break on touch devices.

interaction.title: Infinite Scroll: Use With Care
interaction.summary: Infinite scroll breaks back/forward and footer access. Prefer paginated load-more.

interaction.title: Loading States: Match Final Layout
interaction.summary: Skeletons should approximate the final layout to prevent CLS.

interaction.title: No Modals Inside Modals
interaction.summary: Stacked modals are a UX smell. Use full-screen takeover or in-place editing instead.

interaction.title: Dont Hijack Scroll
interaction.summary: Respect native scroll behavior; don't override speed, direction, or chaining.

motion.title: Motion Easing
motion.summary: Use ease-out for entrances, ease-in for exits, ease-in-out for moves. Avoid linear except for loops.

motion.title: Motion Has Purpose
motion.summary: Animation communicates: state changes, hierarchy, spatial relationships. Decorative motion is noise.

motion.title: Staggered Animations
motion.summary: Stagger 30-50ms between items to imply sequence. >100ms feels slow.

motion.title: No Auto-Play Looping Motion
motion.summary: Looping animations next to text are distracting; pause when user is reading.

motion.title: Respect prefers-reduced-motion
motion.summary: Disable non-essential motion when user prefers reduced motion.

motion.title: Spatial Continuity
motion.summary: Animate elements between states so users track them; don't snap-cut.

motion.title: Animate Transform and Opacity Only
motion.summary: Animating layout properties (width, height, top, left) causes jank. Use transform and opacity.

content.title: Disclose AI-Generated Content
content.summary: When AI generates user-facing content, label it clearly.

content.title: Button Labels Describe Action
content.summary: Buttons say what they do, in user terms.

content.title: Consistent Terminology
content.summary: Use the same word for the same concept everywhere.

content.title: Destructive Action Copy
content.summary: Be explicit. Spell out what will happen and what is irreversible.

content.title: Empty States Teach
content.summary: Empty states are onboarding moments. Tell user what goes here, why, and how to start.

content.title: Error Message Anatomy
content.summary: Problem + cause + solution. No blame. No codes alone.

content.title: Honest Marketing Copy
content.summary: Don't oversell, fake urgency, or use deceptive scarcity claims.

content.title: Internationalization Ready
content.summary: Don't bake assumptions about text length, direction, or pluralization.

content.title: Labels, Not Placeholder-Only
content.summary: Persistent visible labels. Placeholders are hints, not labels.

content.title: Loading Copy
content.summary: Brief, calm. 'Loading...' is fine. Long loads can show what's happening.

content.title: Number and Date Formatting
content.summary: Use locale-aware formatting. Right-align numbers in tables.

content.title: Plain Language
content.summary: Write at a grade 6-8 reading level for general audiences.

content.title: Title Case vs Sentence Case
content.summary: Pick one and stick to it. Sentence case is more modern and easier to read.

content.title: Honest Truncation
content.summary: Long content needs truncation strategy: ellipsis with full content on hover/expand.

content.title: Voice and Tone
content.summary: Define a voice (consistent personality) and tone (varies by context).

forms.title: Group Related Fields
forms.summary: Use headings, fieldsets, or whitespace to group related inputs.

forms.title: Helpful Help Text
forms.summary: Persistent help text for non-obvious fields, below the input.

forms.title: Use Correct Input Types
forms.summary: type='email' / 'tel' / 'number' / 'date' triggers correct keyboards and validation.

forms.title: Form Length: Ask for Less
forms.summary: Every field is friction. Cut anything not strictly necessary.

forms.title: Password UX
forms.summary: Show/hide toggle. Real-time strength feedback. Allow paste.

forms.title: Prevent Form Data Loss
forms.summary: Save drafts. Warn before navigation. Restore on accidental refresh.

forms.title: Mark Required Clearly
forms.summary: Mark required fields with text 'Required' or '*' + legend. Don't rely on color alone.

forms.title: Default to Single Column
forms.summary: Single-column forms are faster to scan and complete.

forms.title: Success State After Submission
forms.summary: Confirm submission clearly. Don't just refresh.

forms.title: Validation Timing
forms.summary: Validate on blur (after user finishes), not on every keystroke. Re-validate on input after first error.
